Notes.Text:
This update for trivy fixes the following issues:

Update to version 0.76.2.

Security issues fixed:

- CVE-2026-97045: golang.org/x/net/html: missing checks during ancestor namespace transitions when rendering raw
  text can cause parser differentials (bsc#1289868).
- CVE-2026-116585,CVE-2026-116586,CVE-2026-116587: github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4: multiple security issues in
  github.com/go-jose/go-jose before 4.1.6 (bsc#1288377).

Other updates and bugfixes:

- Update `x/sys` to 0.50.0 to fix ppc64le syscall handling regression.
- Version 0.76.2:
 * fix(deps): bump `golang.org/x/net` from 0.61.0 to 0.62.0 [backport: release/v0.76] (#11554)
 * chore(deps): bump the common group across 1 directory with 14 updates [backport: release/v0.76] (#11555)
 * fix(deps): bump `github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4` from 4.1.5 to 4.1.6 [backport: release/v0.76] (#11553)
 * fix(deps): bump `alpine` to 3.24.3 in container images [backport: release/v0.76] (#11551)

Vulnerabilities.Description: Go JOSE provides an implementation of the Javascript Object Signing and Encryption set of standards in Go, including support for JSON Web Encryption (JWE), JSON Web Signature (JWS), and JSON Web Token (JWT) standards. Prior to 4.1.5, decrypting untrusted JWE ciphertext with A128CBC-HS256, A192CBC-HS384, or A256CBC-HS512 can pass an empty ciphertext buffer to CBC-HMAC unpadding. Insufficient validation allows the empty buffer to be indexed, causing a panic and denial of service. Applications that decrypt attacker-controlled ciphertext with one of these content-encryption algorithms are affected. This issue is fixed in version 4.1.5.

Go JOSE provides an implementation of the Javascript Object Signing and Encryption set of standards in Go, including support for JSON Web Encryption (JWE), JSON Web Signature (JWS), and JSON Web Token (JWT) standards. Prior to 4.1.5, parsing attacker-controlled JSON through go-jose allows deeply nested arrays or objects to exceed Go's stack limit. The resulting stack overflow crashes the application and permits denial of service in applications that parse untrusted JSON through go-jose. This issue is fixed in version 4.1.5.

Go JOSE provides an implementation of the Javascript Object Signing and Encryption set of standards in Go, including support for JSON Web Encryption (JWE), JSON Web Signature (JWS), and JSON Web Token (JWT) standards. Prior to 4.1.6, go-jose parses attacker-controlled RSA modulus and prime values from JWKs without enforcing size and consistency bounds before passing them to crypto/rsa.PrivateKey.Validate. On Go 1.24 and later, crafted large or degenerate RSA parameters can make that validation consume cubic CPU time, allowing remote denial of service in applications that parse JWKs from untrusted sources. This issue is fixed in version 4.1.6.

In childTextNodesAreLiteral, walking up the tree previously stopped at the nearest foreign ancestor once an HTML integration point was found. However, that integration point may itself be a descendant of an element that was foster-parented into a foreign namespace (such as <mglyph> or <malignmark> fostered under <mtext>), causing a parser to resolve the subtree in a different foreign namespace upon re-parsing the rendered output. Continue walking the full ancestor chain and verify that every transition from a non-empty namespace occurs at an HTML integration point before emitting literal text.
